sentences.text:
D.V.Krishna Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 20
January, 2023

Author: Ninala Jayasurya
Bench: Ninala Jayasurya
In The High Court Of Andhra Pradesh :: Amaravati
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Ninala Jayasurya
 Writ Petition No.1272 of 2023
Between:-
D.V.Krishna Reddy
 ..... Petitioner
 and
The State of Andhra Pradesh, Rep. by its Principal Secretary,
Revenue Department, Secretariat Buildings, Velagapudi,
Amaravathi, and others
 ..... Respondents
Counsel for the petitioner : M/s.K.V.L. Narasimha Rao
Counsel for R.1 to R.4 : The G.P. for Revenue
Order:

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh :: Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 4.
With their consent, the writ petition is being disposed of, at the stage of admission.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, with reference to the averments made in the writ petition,
advanced arguments, inter alia contending that the respondents are taking steps to dispossess the petitioner from the land of an extent of Ac.0.17 cents in survey No.22/3 situated in Soniganipalli Revenue Village, Santipuram Mandal, Chittoor District, in high-handed manner, without issuing any notice to the petitioner or without following due process of law.
He submits that the petitioner and, prior to him, his vendors are in occupation and enjoyment of the said extent of land for more than ten decades.

He submits that even if the respondents want to make use of the said land, they have to take action under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As the respondents are trying to dispossess the petitioner from the subject matter property, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner is constrained to approach this Court seeking appropriate directions.

3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue, on the other hand, submits that even as per the writ petition averments, the petitioner is enjoying the subject matter property as an encroacher and, therefore, he is not entitled to any compensation as pleaded by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

He further submits that the respondents would take appropriate action by following due D.V.Krishna Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117190410/
1 process of law i.e., by issuing notice under the Andhra Pradesh Land Encroachment Act, 1977 (for short, the A.P.L.E. Act).

entities.text: D.V.Krishna Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Government Pleader submits that no orders as sought for by the petitioner may be granted.
4. This Court has considered the submissions made and perused the material on record.

In view of the undisputed position that the petitioner is an encroacher of the subject matter property, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition, leaving it open to the respondent-Authorities to initiate appropriate action under the provisions of the A.P.L.E. Act and give due opportunity to the petitioner before taking any further action in the matter.
Till appropriate orders under the provisions of the said Act are passed, no coercive action in respect of the property in question shall be resorted to.
5. With the above direction, the writ petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, all pending applications shall stand closed.
__ JUSTICE NINALA JAYASURYA January 20, 2023
